title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: KMP
tiers.description: Non-Executive Directors of the Company and Senior Executives (including the Managing Director), as determined by the Board from time to time. All substantive prohibitions (inside information, prohibited periods, short-term dealing, short selling, using securities as loan security) apply to this tier.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors including the MD; distinguished for the notification chain (Chairman, Deputy Chairman or MD, and CFO or Company Secretary) and for exceptional-circumstances clearance requests, which go to the Chairman (or MD in his absence).

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Senior Executives excluding the MD; distinguished for the notification chain (Company Secretary, CFO or MD) and for exceptional-circumstances clearance requests, which go to the MD (or Chairman in his absence). Also referred to conflict-checking with the investment team before dealing in other companies' securities.

tiers.name: Non-Executive Directors
tiers.description: Distinguished from Senior Executives only for the conflict-check process on dealing in other companies' securities (self-assessed, contacting the investment team only if a potential conflict is identified).

tiers.name: third party with reportable interest
tiers.description: A third party in relation to whom a KMP has a reportable interest in the Company's securities as defined by the ASX Listing Rules and Corporations Act due to a relationship with that party; the KMP must use reasonable endeavours to ensure the third party complies with this policy as if it were a KMP.

definitions.hedging_definition: using financial products to protect against or limit the risk associated with unvested Company securities (hedging)

windows.end_anchor: the calendar day after the Company's announcement of its interim financial results
the calendar day after the Company's announcement of its final financial results

windows.start_anchor: seven calendar days prior to the scheduled Board meeting to consider the quarterly dividend
windows.end_anchor: close of the calendar day after the Company's announcement of the quarterly dividend

windows.end_anchor: end of the pricing period for that capital management event

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may impose other periods when KMP are prohibited from dealing because inside information may exist (4.2). The policy does not state whether such additional periods are confidential.

rules.detail: No definition of 'securities' or 'dealing' extends to third-party derivatives or financial products, and derivatives are not otherwise mentioned; the policy is silent on OTC derivatives over the Company's securities.
The Company has no equity-based remuneration schemes, so there are no unvested Company securities held by KMP, and the policy expressly declines to impose a hedging restriction for that reason.
rules.evidence: The Company does not operate any equity-based remuneration schemes. As such, there is no need to have restrictions in place to prohibit KMP from using financial products to protect against or limit the risk associated with unvested Company securities (hedging).

rules.detail: The policy's only reference to hedging (2.6) concerns unvested plan securities, which do not exist because the Company has no equity-based remuneration scheme. Hedging of ordinarily-held, market-acquired securities is not otherwise addressed.
No prepaid forward, collar-monetisation or similar structure is named, and there is no broad dealing definition sweeping such arrangements in.
Outright ban on short-selling the Company's securities.
rules.evidence: KMP must not engage in short-selling of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
CFDs and other financial products are not mentioned or defined anywhere in the policy.

Outright ban on using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements, with no clearance route or exemption; KMP must also use best endeavours to avoid conflicts arising from margin loans over other securities.
rules.evidence: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.

rules.detail: The prohibition extends beyond margin lending to using the Company's securities as security for 'other loans' generally, i.e. any encumbrance in support of financing, with no exemption authority stated.
rules.evidence: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.

rules.detail: Complete, unconditional ban on any secured financing arrangement using the Company's securities as collateral, not limited to margin loans; no clearance route, waiver, or exemption authority is provided anywhere in the policy.
rules.evidence: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.

rules.detail: Intention-based ban on short-term dealing; no fixed numeric period is given, only that dealings must be for investment purposes and holdings must be for 'a reasonable period' rather than active, prompt or repetitive trading.
rules.evidence: KMP must not deal in the Company's securities for short-term purposes. Dealings in the Company's securities must be undertaken for investment purposes and not for trading, that is, the intention in undertaking transactions should be to hold the Company's securities for a reasonable period rather than actively, promptly or repetitively buying and selling them.

clearance.approver: Chairman, Deputy Chairman or the MD, and either the CFO or Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: The Chairman, Deputy Chairman or the MD and either the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) or Company Secretary must be given prior notice of proposed transactions by Directors (including the MD) in the Company's securities.
The Company Secretary, CFO or MD must be given prior notice of proposed transactions by Senior Executives (excluding the MD) in the Company's securities.

clearance.approver: Chairman (or in his absence the MD)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (copied on approval; maintains record)
clearance.evidence: by Directors (including the MD) to the Chairman (or in his absence the MD) ... Approval will be given in writing (including via email) and copied to the Company Secretary who shall maintain a record of all such approvals. Such approval will be for 5 business days beginning the business day after approval is given.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (copied on approval; maintains record)
clearance.evidence: by Senior Executives (excluding the MD) to the MD (or in his absence the Chairman).

exceptions.evidence: A KMP may be in severe financial difficulty if they have a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the Company's securities.

A circumstance will be considered exceptional if the KMP in question is required by a court order to transfer or sell the Company's securities or there is some other overriding legal requirement for them to do so.

exemption_authority: None beyond the Exceptional Circumstances clearance in section 5 (severe financial difficulty, or a court order/overriding legal requirement), which only permits a sale (not a purchase) during a prohibited period, is approved in writing per section 7.3, and is valid for 5 business days. There is no waiver mechanism anywhere in the policy for the outright bans on short-term dealing, short selling, or using the Company's securities as security for a loan.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no equity scheme, so no hedging carve-out needed
bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company does not operate any equity-based remuneration schemes. As such, there is no need to have restrictions in place to prohibit KMP from using financial products to protect against or limit the risk associated with unvested Company securities (hedging).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is not a permission to hedge; it simply notes unvested securities do not exist at Djerriwarrh. All KMP-held shares are ordinary market-acquired ('vested, unrestricted') holdings, so a collar would need to be assessed against the general dealing prohibitions rather than any hedging-specific carve-out, and that assessment is largely silent.

bespoke_clauses.topic: outright ban on using shares as security
bespoke_clauses.clause: KMP are prohibited from using the Company's securities as security for margin lending arrangements or other loans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an absolute, unqualified ban with no clearance route, exemption authority, or carve-out anywhere in the policy; the loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is squarely prohibited for all KMP.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Section 3 lists specific exclusions from the policy (superannuation transfers, discretionary managed funds, Board-approved pro rata offers, no change of beneficial interest, trustee trading, takeover acceptance, gifts, family transactions) but includes no carve-out for a disposal resulting from a secured lender or financier exercising rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because secured financing is banned outright, the policy has no provision addressing a lender's enforcement sale, so a bank collar-related forced sale would have no protected route out of a prohibited period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the intention in undertaking transactions should be to hold the Company's securities for a reasonable period rather than actively, promptly or repetitively buying and selling them.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Absence of a fixed month threshold gives the Company discretion to characterise a collar's term as too short if it resembles trading rather than investment.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the purposes of sections 7.1 to 7.3, no KMP may be the recipient of the prior notification of their own transaction or be the approver of their own transaction involving exceptional circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Ensures a genuine second signature is needed on any exceptional-circumstances sale clearance connected to a collar (e.g. to fund a margin call or hardship), though the policy does not specify who approves the Chairman's own exceptional-circumstances request.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Such approval will be for 5 business days beginning the business day after approval is given.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any cleared sale (e.g. to unwind or settle a permitted structure) must be executed within a narrow 5-business-day window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may be required to notify the existence of exceptional circumstances to the Australian Securities Exchange.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A hardship-driven sale connected to a funded position could trigger public ASX disclosure of the exceptional circumstances behind it.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Section 2.5 imposes a blanket, unconditional prohibition on KMP using Djerriwarrh securities as security for 'margin lending arrangements or other loans', with no clearance route, exemption authority, or carve-out anywhere in the policy, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares is prohibited outright for all KMP (Non-Executive Directors and Senior Executives including the MD). The Company has no equity-based remuneration schemes, so there is no unvested or holding-locked stock and no hedging-specific restriction applies for that reason, but the option legs of a collar are not otherwise addressed by any derivatives, financial-products or dealing-definition provision, leaving their treatment genuinely silent. Even setting the financing ban aside, entry, unwind or settlement of any leg would need to occur outside the fixed half-year, full-year, quarterly-dividend and capital-management-event prohibited periods (and any ad hoc blackout), and would need to reflect a 'reasonable period' holding intention rather than short-term trading. The only relief mechanism is a narrow Exceptional Circumstances clearance permitting a sale (not a purchase) for severe financial hardship or a court order, valid for 5 business days and requiring written approval from the Chairman or MD as applicable; this creates no pathway around the prohibited secured-financing leg. Overall, the funded collar fails on the absolute ban on encumbering Djerriwarrh shares to secure any loan.
